title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a fragment of the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes, Grothendieck's unpublished Tannakian programme. It is misfiled: the neighbouring pages are a Bourbaki-style redaction of the ODE existence theorem and are unrelated.

Setting, as far as the page lets one infer it.
- A appears to be a ring of integral adeles, prod_l Z_l, apparently including the place p and an archimedean component A_inf = R.
- C(A,T') denotes realization categories with coefficients in A, each with a Tate object T. The local pieces are:
  - C(A_p,T_p), which is crystalline-type: Frobenius acts, and a margin mentions 'cristal sur F_p'.
  - C(A_inf,T_inf), which is Hodge-type.
- A 'catégorie de Demazure de type xi in Br(Q)' seems to be Grothendieck's ad hoc name for a Q-linear tensor category with a Tate object whose gerbe has Brauer class xi. Br(Q) = H^2(Q,G_m) is plausibly the class obtained by pushing the gerbe along the weight/Tate character.

Step 1. For the algebraic closure of F_p, Grothendieck has constructed (on earlier, missing pages) a set T(F_p-bar). He asserts it is a canonical torsor under H^1(A,mu_2) = prod_l Z_l^*/Z_l^{*2}. By Kummer theory and triviality of Pic of local rings, H^1_fppf(Z_l,mu_2) = Z_l^*/Z_l^{*2}. These factors are naturally the automorphism classes of a realization functor at l, modulo squares: changing the trivialization of the rank-one Tate object by a unit, up to squares.

Step 2. A priori T depends on F_p-bar. To descend it to F_p he computes the action of Frobenius F in Z^ = Gal(F_p-bar/F_p). The action is the product of three pieces:
- the usual (cyclotomic) action on the l-adic components, where Frobenius acts on A'(1) via p;
- the crystalline Frobenius on C(A_p,T_p);
- the trivial action on C(A_inf,T_inf).
The resulting element is a previously computed 'classe (p,F,p)', which he says is trivial. Hence F acts trivially, and one gets a canonical torsor T over F_p under H^1(A,mu_2).

Step 3 (NB). This suggests that T is the obstruction to a canonical (quasi-)trivialization of a mu_2-structure on A, attached to isomorphism classes. He then begins a construction:
- Consider pairs (C,alpha), where C is a Demazure category of type xi with Tate object T_C = T.
- alpha is an equivalence class of identifications of (C,T)_{Z_p} with the standard (C(Z_p),T(Z_p)), taken modulo equivalences coming from Pic(Z_p).
- Equivalently, alpha is a section of the mu_2-torsor obtained from the Isom-torsor with group Isom(C(Z_p),T(Z_p)) = Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} by extension of structure group to mu_2.
- He states that every C admits such an alpha, and starts comparing two pairs (C,alpha), (C',alpha'); the text breaks off there.
- Margins introduce a 'Brauer group' Br(M,g) of classes of such (C,T) relative to (M,g) and (M_p,g). They also note that concretely alpha is given by crystal-type data over F_p and a square class of the ring Z_p.

Overall purpose: control the sign/square-class ambiguity in the realizations of the Tate object. This is the mu_2 (orientation, 'choice of i or of sqrt p') ambiguity, in order to rigidify fibre functors and realization functors for motives over finite fields and over Q.
errors: For p = 2 (or l = 2), Z_2^*/Z_2^{*2} has order 4, so it is not canonically mu_2. The 'extension of structure group to mu_2' needs a chosen homomorphism Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} -> mu_2, which is canonical (the Legendre symbol) only for odd p.

The claim that Frobenius acts trivially is not justified on this page; it rests on an earlier-computed class (p,F,p). Naively, Frobenius acts on the l-adic Tate object through p, and p is a non-square in Z_l^* for roughly half of the primes l. Triviality must therefore come from a square/weight normalisation or a compensation not visible here, so this is a gap to check.

The identification of H^1(A,mu_2) with a product over places silently uses that Pic is trivial for the (infinite) product of local rings. It also omits the archimedean factor R^*/R^{*2} unless it is included in the product.

ideas.what: The sign/square-class ambiguity of the realizations of the Tate object, organised as a canonical torsor under prod_v Z_v^*/Z_v^{*2} (an adelic mu_2-cohomology group)
ideas.modern_name: Orientation (2*pi*i / sqrt p sign) torsor for realizations of Q(1); mu_2-ambiguity of fibre functors on motives over finite fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles, 1982); Milne ('Motives over finite fields', 1994); Langlands–Rapoport (1987)

ideas.what: Galois descent of the torsor from F_p-bar to F_p by computing the Frobenius action componentwise: cyclotomic at l, crystalline Frobenius at p, trivial at infinity
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius action on a system of realizations (l-adic, crystalline, Hodge)

ideas.what: Tensor categories with Tate object classified by a Brauer class xi in Br(Q) ('catégorie de Demazure de type xi')
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian gerbes and their Brauer/H^2 class via the weight cocharacter

ideas.what: Rigidifying data alpha: a class of integral p-adic (crystalline) equivalences modulo Pic(Z_p), pushed to mu_2; and a 'Brauer group' Br(M,g) of such categories
ideas.modern_name: Integral p-adic/crystalline fibre functor rigidification; relative Brauer group of Tannakian categories

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates, already in 1965, a canonical mu_2-torsor over the integral adeles (place p and infinity included) that measures the square-class ambiguity of identifying realization categories with Tate object. He shows it descends to F_p and conjectures it is the obstruction to a canonical trivialization. The comparison of pairs (C,alpha), (C',alpha') breaks off.
missed.quote: Ceci suggère qu'il y a une ... trivialisation ... de μ2 sur A, dont T serait l'obstruction
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The sign/sqrt(p) ambiguities are a known technical nuisance in motives over finite fields, the Langlands–Rapoport conjecture and in fibre functors on Weil-number categories. A packaging as a single adelic mu_2-torsor with explicit Frobenius descent predates Milne and Deligne's treatments and is not credited to Grothendieck.

missed.claim: The page combines local square classes at all places (including p via crystals and infinity) into one torsor. This is implicitly a Hilbert-reciprocity-type structure attached to the Tate motive, linked to Brauer classes of Tannakian categories over Q.
missed.quote: C est une catégorie de Demazure de type ξ∈Br(Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a reciprocity or obstruction-theoretic description of the Brauer class of motivic gerbes in terms of local orientation data. I am unaware of this being written down in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an early (1965) unpublished, motivic-Galois-theoretic treatment of the mu_2/sign ambiguity of Tate-object realizations as an adelic torsor with Frobenius descent and an obstruction interpretation, a theme later handled by Deligne, Milne and Langlands–Rapoport. It is fragmentary, partly illegible, and depends on missing pages, so its precise content is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: '(ℓ premiers petits[?])' under the product is more likely '(y compris p et ∞)', i.e. the product runs over all places including p and infinity.
The parenthetical after 'Cette opération se fait via' likely reads '(opérations habituelles sur A'(1), [F] opère par p)', not 'variables habituelles'.
'opération de Ẑ ∋ F' and 'classe (p,F,p)': F denotes the Frobenius generator of Ẑ.
The neighbouring pages (ODE existence theorem) are unrelated, so this sheet is misplaced in the scan order.
